body.translated_text: The Chanting of Names (<s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>) of the Non-dual Ultimate Truth (<s>Advaya-paramārtha</s>)
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious great lord <s>Mañjunātha</s>!

children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>,
the supreme tamer of the untamed,
the hero victorious over the three worlds,
the king of secrets, lord of the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt),
with fully-awakened lotus eyes,
with a face [blooming] like an opened lotus,
brandishing the supreme <s>vajra</s>
in his own hand again and again,
together with <s>Bhṛkuṭī-taraṅga</s> and the others —
infinite <s>Vajrapāṇis</s>,
heroic tamers of the untamed,
of heroic and fearsome forms,
brandishing with their own hands
<s>vajras</s> with flashing tips,
supreme in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and great compassion,
acting for the welfare of the world,
joyful, pleased, and delighted in mind,
bearing the forms of wrathful bodies,
performing the deeds of a <s>Buddha</s>, protectors —
together [with them], with bodies bowed in homage,
having bowed to the protector, the perfectly awakened one,
the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
standing before him with palms joined,
he spoke these words:
'For my benefit, for my welfare,
out of compassion for me, O all-pervading one,
that I may obtain the awakening of the Net of <s>Māyā</s> (<s>Māyājālābhisaṃbodhi</s>) —
so that I may become one who has attained it,
for those sunk in the mire of ignorance,
their minds troubled by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
for the benefit of all beings,
for the attainment of the unsurpassed fruit —
may the perfectly awakened one reveal [it],
the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the teacher, the world's guru,
knower of the truth of the great assembly,
supreme knower of the faculties and dispositions [of beings] —
of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s knowledge-body,
of [him with] the great <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance), lord of speech,
of <s>Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva</s> (the knowledge-being <s>Mañjuśrī</s>),
of the self-born knowledge-form —
the supreme chanting of names (<s>nāmasaṃgīti</s>),
of profound meaning, noble meaning, great meaning, incomparable, auspicious,
auspicious at beginning, middle, and end,
[this chanting of names] —
which was spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past,
which will be spoken by those of the future,
and which the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> of the present
speak again and again,
which in the great <s>tantra</s> of the Net of <s>Māyā</s> (<s>Māyājāla</s>)
is also chanted herein
by the great joyful <s>Vajradharas</s>,
by immeasurable holders of <s>mantras</s> —
I too shall hold this [chanting]
with firm resolve until final passing,
so that I, O protector, may become
the upholder of the secret of all perfectly awakened ones.
I shall proclaim it to beings
according to their particular dispositions,
for the destruction of all afflictions without remainder,
for the elimination of all ignorance without remainder.'
Having thus petitioned, the lord of secrets,
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, [addressing] the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
with palms joined,
stood before him with body inclined.

body.translated_text: Thus are the sixteen verses of the knowledge of petition.

children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>,
the perfectly awakened one, the best of bipeds,
extending his broad, ample,
and auspicious tongue from his own mouth,
displaying a smile that purifies
the three lower realms for [all] worlds,
that illuminates the three worlds,
that is the teaching [subduing] the four <s>Māras</s> as enemies,
filling the three worlds
with a <s>Brāhmī</s> (divine), sweet voice,
he addressed the lord of secrets,
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of great strength:
'Excellent, O glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>!
Excellent [is it] of you, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>,
that you, for the welfare of the world,
endowed with great compassion,
are eager to hear from me
the chanting of names of great purpose,
pure, destroying sins,
of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>'s knowledge-body.
Therefore, excellent — I shall teach it.
Listen, O lord of the <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret beings)!
Listen with one-pointed mind!'
'Excellent, O <s>Bhagavān</s>!' [he replied].

body.translated_text: Thus are the six verses of the knowledge of the response.

children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>,
surveying the entire great <s>mantra</s>-family,
the family of <s>mantra</s>-knowledge holders,
the three families —
the worldly and supramundane family,
the great family of world and non-world,
and the foremost family of the great <s>mudrā</s> (seal),
the great family of the <s>Mahā-uṣṇīṣa</s> —

body.translated_text: Thus are the two verses of the knowledge of surveying the six families.

children.translated_text: He spoke this verse
conjoined with the six <s>mantra</s>-kings,
whose nature is the arising of non-duality,
whose nature is non-arising — of the Lord of Speech:

children.text: a ā i ī u ū e ai
children.translated_text: A Ā I Ī U Ū E AI

children.text: o au aṃ aḥ sthito hṛdi
children.translated_text: O AU AṂ AḤ — established in the heart.
'I am the knowledge-form, the <s>Buddha</s>,
of the <s>Buddhas</s> abiding in the three times.'
<s>Oṃ</s>! To the one whose form is the <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge that cuts suffering with the sharp <s>vajra</s> —
to <s>Ārapacana</s>, the knowledge-body, lord of speech — homage to you!

body.translated_text: Thus are the three verses of the stages of the <s>Māyājālābhisaṃbodhi</s> (Awakening through the Net of Māyā).

children.translated_text: As the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>,
the perfectly awakened one, born from the syllable A,
the syllable A is foremost among all phonemes,
of great meaning, the supreme imperishable.
The great breath (<s>mahāprāṇa</s>), [he is] non-arising,
free from verbal utterance,
the foremost cause of all speech,
the most luminous of all words.
The great festival of great passion,
creating delight for all beings,
the great festival of great hatred,
the great enemy of all afflictions,
the great festival of great delusion,
the destroyer of the delusion of confused minds,
the great festival of great wrath,
the great enemy of great wrath, the great one,
the great festival of great greed,
the destroyer of all greed,
the great desire, the great bliss,
the great delight, the great joy,
of great form, of great body,
of great color, of great physique,
of great name, of great nobility,
of great and vast <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle),
bearing the weapon of great <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
the great goad for afflictions, the leader,
of great glory, of great fame,
of great light, of great splendor,
the learned one bearing great <s>māyā</s> (illusion),
the accomplisher of the purpose of great <s>māyā</s>,
delighting in the play of great <s>māyā</s>,
the great magician of <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Indrajāla</s>,
the supreme lord of great generosity (<s>dāna</s>),
the leader bearing great moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>),
the steadfast one bearing great patience (<s>kṣānti</s>),
of great energy (<s>vīrya</s>) and valor,
established in great meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and <s>samādhi</s>,
bearing the body of great <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
of great strength, of great skillful means (<s>upāya</s>),
of [great] aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>), an ocean of knowledge,
made of great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), immeasurable,
of great compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), of supreme intelligence,
of great <s>prajñā</s>, of great intellect,
of great skillful means, of great accomplishment,
endowed with great <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) and strength,
of great speed, of great swiftness,
of great supernatural power, called the great lord,
of great strength and valor,
the shatterer of the great mountain of existence,
the bearer of the great <s>vajra</s>, solid,
of great ferocity, of great wrath,
the terrifier of great fear,
the protector supreme in great <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge),
the guru supreme in great <s>mantras</s>,
mounted upon the vehicle of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,
supreme in the method of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus are the fourteen verses of the knowledge of the <s>Vajradhātu-maṇḍala</s>.

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Mahāvairocana</s>,
the great silent sage, the great <s>Muni</s>,
arisen from the method of the great <s>mantra</s>,
whose nature is the method of the great <s>mantra</s>,
who has attained the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
whose support is the ten <s>pāramitās</s>,
whose purity is the ten <s>pāramitās</s>,
whose method is the ten <s>pāramitās</s>,
the lord of the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), the protector,
established on the ten <s>bhūmis</s>,
of purified nature through the ten knowledges,
the upholder of purity through the ten knowledges,
of ten aspects, whose purpose is the ten meanings,
the lord of sages, possessing the ten powers, the all-pervading one,
the accomplisher of all universal purposes,
the great master of the ten aspects,
beginningless, whose nature is free from elaboration,
of pure nature, whose nature is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
a speaker of truth, one who acts as he speaks,
one who acts as [he declares], of non-other speech,
non-dual, a proclaimer of non-duality,
abiding at the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>),
whose lion's roar is selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>),
terrifying to the deer of false teachers,
going everywhere, of unfailing course,
swift as the mind of a <s>Tathāgata</s>,
the conqueror, the vanquisher of foes, the victorious one,
the universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), of great power,
the chief of assemblies, the teacher of assemblies,
the lord of assemblies, the master of assemblies, the sovereign,
of great majesty, the foremost,
not led by others, of great method,
the lord of speech, the master of words, the eloquent one,
the lord of speech, of infinite utterance,
of true speech, a speaker of truth,
a teacher of the four [noble] truths,
the irreversible one (<s>avaivartika</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmī</s>),
the sword (<s>khaḍga</s>), the solitary leader (<s>pratyeka-nāyaka</s>),
gone forth through various modes of liberation,
the sole cause of the great elements,
the <s>Arhat</s>, whose outflows are exhausted, a <s>bhikṣu</s>,
free from passion, with senses conquered,
having reached security, having reached fearlessness,
cooled, untroubled,
endowed with knowledge and conduct,
the well-gone one (<s>Sugata</s>), the supreme knower of the world,
free from 'mine,' free from ego,
established in the method of the two truths,
abiding at the further shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
having accomplished his task, standing on firm ground,
expelled by the knowledge of absolute isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>),
the cleaver with the weapon of <s>prajñā</s>,
the true <s>Dharma</s>, the king of <s>Dharma</s>, radiant,
the supreme maker of world-light,
the lord of <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-king,
the teacher of the path to the highest good,
of accomplished purpose, of accomplished resolve,
free from all conceptual resolve,
free from conceptualization, the imperishable element,
the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), supreme, immutable,
meritorious, an accumulation of merit,
knowledge, the great mine of knowledge,
possessed of knowledge, knower of being and non-being,
furnished with the two accumulations,
eternal, universal sovereign, a <s>yogin</s>,
meditation itself, the object of meditation, lord of thoughts,
to be known by oneself, immovable,
the supreme and primal one, bearer of the three bodies (<s>trikāya</s>),
the <s>Buddha</s> whose nature is the five bodies,
the all-pervading one whose nature is the five knowledges,
crowned with the five <s>Buddhas</s> as his own nature,
bearing the five eyes, free from attachment,
the father of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the supreme and best son of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
born from the womb of <s>prajñā</s>-existence,
the <s>Dharma</s>-womb, the ender of existence,
of solid single essence, of <s>vajra</s> nature,
just-born, lord of the world,
born from the sky, self-born,
the great fire of <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge,
<s>Vairocana</s>, of great radiance,
the light of knowledge, the illuminator,
the lamp of the world, the torch of knowledge,
of great brilliance, luminous,
the king of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), the foremost lord of <s>mantras</s>,
the king of <s>mantras</s>, the accomplisher of great purpose,
the great <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, the wondrous <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>,
the all-seeing one, lord of the sky,
foremost in being the self-nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the eye of joy for the world,
of universal form, the creator,
worthy of worship, worthy of honor, the great sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>),
the holder of the three families, the <s>mantra</s>-knower,
the upholder of the great assembly <s>mantra</s>,
the best bearer of the three jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>),
the supreme teacher of the three vehicles,
the unfailing noose (<s>Amoghapāśa</s>), the victorious one,
the <s>vajra</s>-noose, the great seizer,
the <s>vajra</s>-hook, the great noose,
terrifying as <s>Vajra-bhairava</s>,

body.translated_text: Thus are the twenty-five verses minus a quarter-verse of the knowledge of the pure, thoroughly purified <s>Dharmadhātu</s>.

children.translated_text: The king of wrath, six-faced, terrifying,
six-eyed, six-armed, powerful,
terrible with fangs, a skeleton,
<s>Halāhala</s> (deadly poison), hundred-faced,
<s>Yamāntaka</s> (the ender of Death), the king of obstacles,
of <s>vajra</s>-speed, terrifying,
the <s>vajra</s>-proclaimer, the heart-<s>vajra</s>,
the <s>māyā</s>-<s>vajra</s>, of great belly,
the lord of the <s>vajra</s>, of <s>vajra</s>-origin,
the <s>vajra</s>-sphere, like the sky,
the immovable one of single towering matted hair,
wearing a moist elephant skin as garment,
the cry 'Hā Hā!' — of great terror,
the cry 'Hī Hī!' — fearsome,
the great laugh 'Aṭṭahāsa,' the great laughter,
the <s>vajra</s>-laugh, of great roar,
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great being,
<s>Vajrarāja</s>, the great bliss,
<s>Vajracaṇḍa</s>, the great delight,
<s>Vajra-hūṃkāra</s>, the maker of the Hūṃ sound,
the bearer of <s>vajra</s>-arrow weapons,
the <s>vajra</s>-sword, the cutter,
the bearer of the <s>viśva-vajra</s> (crossed vajra), the <s>vajra</s>-holder,
the single <s>vajra</s>-holder, the abandoner of battle,
of terrible eyes [blazing] with <s>vajra</s>-flames,
with hair of <s>vajra</s>-flames,
of <s>vajra</s>-possession, of great possession,
the hundred-eyed one, of <s>vajra</s>-eyes,
whose body is sprouting with <s>vajra</s>-hairs,
whose single form is of <s>vajra</s>-hairs,
whose nails begin as millions of <s>vajra</s>-tips,
whose skin is solid <s>vajra</s>-essence,
the glorious bearer of <s>vajra</s>-garlands,
adorned with <s>vajra</s>-ornaments,
the resounding laughter 'Hā Hā Aṭṭahāsa,'
the <s>vajra</s>-sound, the six-syllabled one,
<s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Sweet Voice), the great sound,
the great single sound of the three worlds,
the sound reaching to the limit of the sky-element,
the best among those who have voice.

body.translated_text: Thus are the ten and a quarter verses of the knowledge of the Mirror[-like Wisdom].

children.translated_text: <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), true selflessness,
the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), beyond syllables,
the bull among proclaimers of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
of profound and noble roar,
the <s>Dharma</s>-conch of great sound,
the <s>Dharma</s>-bell of great resonance,
of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without fixed abode (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>),
the <s>Dharma</s>-drum of the ten directions,
formless, yet foremost in having form,
of various forms, mind-made,
the glory of the manifestation of all forms,
the bearer of all reflections without exception,
invincible, called the great lord,
the great sovereign of the triple world,
established on the exalted noble path,
the <s>Dharma</s>-banner, of great arising,
the youthful one of the three worlds,
the elder, the ancient, <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures),
the bearer of the thirty-two marks,
the lovely one, the beautiful one of the three worlds,
the teacher of the world's knowledge and virtues,
the world's teacher, the confident one,
the protector, the savior, the trusted one of the three worlds,
the refuge, the guardian, the unsurpassed one,
whose enjoyment is the expanse of the sky,
the ocean of omniscient knowledge,
the breaker of the egg-shell of ignorance,
the destroyer of the cage of existence,
the one who has pacified all afflictions without remainder,
the one who has crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
crowned with the consecration of knowledge,
the ornament of the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>,
the pacifier of the three sufferings of suffering,
of three ends, infinite, having attained the three liberations,
freed from all obscurations,
having attained equality with space,
having transcended the stain of all afflictions,
having gone to the pathless course of the three times,
the great elephant (<s>nāga</s>) among all beings,
the crest-jewel among those with the crest of virtues,
freed from all conditions,
well-established on the path of space,
the bearer of the great wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>),
the supreme among all jewels, the all-pervading one,
the great wish-fulfilling tree, abundant,
the supreme excellent vessel of good fortune (<s>bhadra-ghaṭa</s>),
the accomplisher of the purpose of all beings, the agent,
the well-wisher, the one tender toward beings,
the knower of good and evil, the knower of time,
the knower of commitments, the committed one, the all-pervading one,
the knower of beings' faculties, the knower of occasions,
skilled in the three liberations,
virtuous, the knower of virtues, the knower of <s>Dharma</s>,
the praised one, the arising of auspiciousness,
the most auspicious of all auspicious things,
fame, fortune, glory, the auspicious one,
the great festival, the great consolation,
the great joy, the great delight,
honor, reverence, prosperity,
gladness, splendor, the lord of glory,
the most excellent, the granter of boons, the best,
worthy of refuge, the supreme refuge,
the foe of great fear, the most eminent,
the destroyer of all fear without remainder,
the crested one (<s>Śikhī</s>), the peacock-plumed one, the matted-haired one,
the one with braids, the shaven-headed one, the one with a crown,
the five-faced one, the five-crested one,
the one crowned with five locks of hair,
the bearer of the great vow, wearing the <s>muñja</s>-grass girdle,
the <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), supreme in vows,
of great austerity, devoted to austerity,
the accomplished one (<s>snātaka</s>), of <s>Gautama</s>'s lineage, the foremost,
the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> himself,
the one who has attained <s>Brahma-nirvāṇa</s>,
liberation, release, the limb of deliverance,
freedom, tranquility, the auspicious one (<s>Śiva</s>),
<s>nirvāṇa</s>, cessation, peace,
the highest good, departure, the one who has reached the end,
the ender of happiness and suffering, the final goal,
dispassion, the exhaustion of conditions,
unconquered, incomparable, unmanifest,
without appearance, without stain,
without parts, all-pervading, pervasive,
subtle, the seed, without outflows,
dustless, free from dust, stainless,
with faults expelled, free from disease,
fully awakened, of awakened nature,
omniscient, all-knowing, the supreme one,
having transcended the nature of consciousness,
bearing the non-dual form of knowledge,
free from conceptualization, without activity,
accomplishing the deeds of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times,
the <s>Buddha</s> without beginning or end,
the primordial <s>Buddha</s> (<s>Ādibuddha</s>), without succession,
the stainless one whose single eye is knowledge,
the knowledge-form, the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
the lord of speech, the great debater,
the king of debaters, the best among debaters.
The foremost and most excellent among speakers,
the lion of debaters, unconquered.
The all-seeing one, the joyful one,
the garland of radiance, the beautiful to behold,
<s>Śrīvatsa</s>, of excellent brilliance, luminous,
with rays of light and dazzling hands of splendor.
The supreme great physician, the best,
the remover of thorns (suffering), unsurpassed,
the tree of all medicines,
the great enemy of the disease of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions).
The ornament of the three worlds, the beloved one,
the glorious one, the circle of stars,
extending to the sky of the ten directions,
of great height like the banner of <s>Dharma</s>.
The one vast umbrella of the world,
the circle of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
the glorious lord of the lotus-dance,
the jewel-umbrella, the great sovereign.
The great king of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
bearing the essential nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great <s>yoga</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the single teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The glory of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel consecration,
the lord and master of all jewels,
the lord of all world-rulers,
the sovereign of all <s>vajra</s>-holders.
The great mind of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the mental course of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the great body of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
The <s>vajra</s>-sun, the great light,
the <s>vajra</s>-moon of stainless radiance,
the great passion born from passionlessness,
blazing with the splendor of universal colors.
The <s>vajra</s> cross-legged seat of the perfectly awakened one,
bearing the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed in the <s>Buddha</s>-assembly,
the glorious one born from the <s>Buddha</s>-lotus,
bearing the treasury of the knowledge of the omniscient.
The king who holds the illusion of the universe,
the great holder of the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,
the <s>vajra</s>-sharp one, the great sword,
the pure one, the supreme imperishable syllable.
The great vehicle that cuts through suffering,
the great weapon of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>Dharma</s>,
the conqueror of conquerors, of <s>vajra</s> profundity,
of <s>vajra</s> intellect, the knower of things as they are.
The fulfiller of all <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
the ornament of all <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
the selflessness of the purified <s>Dharma</s>,
with the heart-light of the moon of perfect knowledge.
The great enterprise of the net of <s>māyā</s> (illusion),
the supreme lord of all <s>tantras</s>,
the complete <s>vajra</s> cross-legged seat,
bearing the body of exhaustive knowledge.
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, of good intellect,
<s>Kṣitigarbha</s>, the support of the world,
the great womb of all <s>Buddhas</s>,
bearing the wheel of universal creation.
Supreme in the own-nature of all existences,
perceiving the own-nature of all existences,
of the nature of non-arising, of universal purpose,
bearing the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>.
Of great wisdom in a single moment,
bearing the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>,
the realization of all <s>dharmas</s>,
the sage of the ultimate reality, of foremost intellect.
Serene, of supremely clear nature,
bearing the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of the perfectly awakened one,
directly perceivable by all <s>Buddhas</s>,
the flame of knowledge, supremely radiant.

body.translated_text: Thus end the forty-two verses on the knowledge of discernment.

children.translated_text: The supreme accomplisher of desired aims,
the purifier of all lower realms,
the supreme being among all sentient beings, the protector,
the liberator of all sentient beings.
The sole hero in the battle against <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the destroyer of the pride of the enemy of ignorance,
the intellect, the bearer of the amorous sentiment, the glorious one,
bearing the forms of the heroic and the terrible.
Swinging hundreds of arm-clubs,
dancing with foot-stamps,
the glorious one with the expanse of a hundred arms,
dancing in the expanse of the sky.
Standing on the surface of the great earth
trampled by the sole of one foot,
standing on the toenail
that has trampled the summit of the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg).
Of single meaning, whose meaning is the non-dual <s>Dharma</s>,
the ultimate truth, the imperishable,
whose meaning is the forms of diverse perceptions,
the continuum of mind and consciousness.
Delighting in the meaning of all existences,
delighting in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), of foremost intellect,
transcending attachment to existence and the rest,
the great delight in the three states of existence.
Pure, white as a bright cloud,
of excellent radiance like the rays of the autumn moon,
with the hue of the orb of the young sun,
with the splendor of nails of great passion.
With hair-tips of excellent sapphire blue,
bearing the tips of great blue locks,
the glory of the rays of great jewels,
the ornament of the <s>Buddha's</s> <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Shaking a hundred world-realms,
of great stride through the <s>ṛddhipāda</s> (bases of supernatural power),
bearing great <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), true,
the king of the four <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundations of mindfulness) <s>samādhis</s>.
Fragrant with the blossoms of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening),
the ocean of the qualities of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
the knower of the method of the <s>Aṣṭāṅgamārga</s> (Eightfold Path),
the knower of the path of the perfectly awakened ones.
Greatly attached to all sentient beings,
yet unattached, like the sky,
born from the minds of all sentient beings,
swift as the minds of all sentient beings.
The knower of the faculties and aims of all sentient beings,
the captivator of the minds of all sentient beings,
the knower of the truth of the meaning of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),
bearing the purity of the five <s>skandhas</s>.
Abiding at the summit of all modes of liberation,
skilled in all modes of liberation,
standing on the path of all modes of liberation,
the teacher of all modes of liberation.
One who has uprooted the twelve limbs of existence,
bearing the purity of the twelve aspects,
of the form of the method of the Four Noble Truths,
bearing the awakening to the eight knowledges.
Whose meaning is the truth of the twelve aspects,
the knower of the reality of the sixteen aspects,
the awakening of the twenty aspects,
the awakened one, the knower of all, the supreme.
The illuminator of immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-emanations,
of myriads of bodies,
the realization in every moment,
the knower of the meaning of every moment of mind.
The illuminator of the world's purpose through the means
and methods of various vehicles,
having emerged through the three vehicles,
established in the fruit of the single vehicle.
Of a nature purified from the realm of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
the destroyer of the realm of <s>karma</s>,
having crossed the ocean of the flood,
having emerged from the wilderness of <s>yoga</s>.
Having well abandoned the afflictions, secondary afflictions, and defilements
together with their latent impressions,
through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
the unfailing accomplisher of the world's purpose.
Whose meaning is the abandonment of all notions,
whose meaning is consciousness, the maker of cessation,
the object of the minds of all sentient beings,
the mental course of all sentient beings.
Abiding within the minds of all sentient beings,
having attained equality with their minds,
the delighter of the minds of all sentient beings,
the delight of the minds of all sentient beings.
The established conclusion, free from error,
devoid of all delusion,
of undoubting intellect, of threefold meaning,
of all meanings, of the nature of the three qualities.
Whose meaning is the five <s>skandhas</s>, of the three times,
the illuminator of every moment,
perfectly awakened in a single moment,
bearing the own-nature of all <s>Buddhas</s>.
Of bodiless body, supreme among bodies,
the illuminator of myriads of bodies,
the displayer of all forms without exception,
<s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel-Banner), the great gem.

body.translated_text: Thus end the twenty-four verses on the knowledge of equality.

children.translated_text: To be awakened to by all the perfectly awakened ones,
the unsurpassed <s>Buddha-bodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening),
without syllables, the source of <s>mantras</s>,
the three families of the great <s>mantras</s>.
The generator of the meaning of all <s>mantras</s>,
the great <s>bindu</s> (drop), without syllables,
the five-syllabled one, the great void,
the void of the <s>bindu</s>, the six-syllabled one.
Of all forms, yet formless,
bearing the half-half of the sixteen <s>bindus</s>,
partless, beyond the division of parts,
bearing the summit of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
Knowing all the arts of all <s>dhyānas</s>,
the knower of the lineage and clan of <s>samādhi</s>,
the body of <s>samādhi</s>, supreme among bodies,
the king of all <s>saṃbhogakāyas</s> (enjoyment-bodies).
The <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation-body), supreme among bodies,
bearing the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>-emanations,
the universal emanation in the ten directions,
the accomplisher of the world's purpose as it truly is.
The god beyond gods, the lord of gods,
the lord of the celestials, the ruler of the <s>Dānavas</s>,
the lord of the immortals, the guru of the gods,
<s>Pramatha</s> (the tormentor), the lord of the <s>Pramathas</s>.
Having crossed beyond the wilderness of existence,
the sole teacher, the guru of the world,
renowned throughout the worlds of the ten directions,
the great lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>.
Clad in the armor of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),
protected by the mail of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion),
with the sword, bow, and arrow of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
the destroyer of the battle of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and ignorance.
The enemy of <s>Māra</s>, the conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, the hero,
the destroyer of the fear of the four <s>Māras</s>,
the vanquisher of the entire army of <s>Māra</s>,
the perfectly awakened one, the leader of the world.
Worthy of salutation, worthy of worship, worthy of homage,
and to be honored always,
most worthy of adoration, to be esteemed,
worthy of obeisance, the supreme guru.
Traversing the three worlds in a single stride,
of a stride extending to the limits of the sky,
possessed of the three knowledges, learned, pure,
possessed of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges) and the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections).
The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the great being,
transcending the world, of great supernatural power,
grounded in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom),
having attained the truth-nature of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).
The knower of the self, the knower of others, the all,
possessed of strength, the foremost individual,
having transcended all comparisons,
the knowable, the supreme lord of knowledge.
The best lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>,
the teacher of the meaning of the four <s>mudrās</s> (seals),
the most worthy of worship by the beings of the worlds
who travel the three paths of liberation.
Of glory purified in the ultimate truth,
the great fortunate one of the three worlds,
the bestower of all prosperity, the glorious one,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the best among the glorious.

body.translated_text: Thus end the fifteen verses on the knowledge of the performance of duties.

children.translated_text: Homage to You, O foremost <s>vajra</s> of boons,
homage to You, O summit of reality,
homage to You, O womb of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
homage to You, O <s>Buddha-bodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening).
Homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-passion,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-desire,
homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-delight,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-joy.
Homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-smile,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-laughter,
homage to You, O <s>Buddha</s>-speech,
homage, homage, O <s>Buddha</s>-nature.
Homage to You, O one born from non-being,
homage to You, O one born from the <s>Buddha</s>,
homage to You, O one born from the sky,
homage to You, O one born from knowledge.
Homage to You, O net of <s>māyā</s> (illusion),
homage to You, O dramatic play of the <s>Buddha</s>,
homage to You among all and for all,
homage to You, O body of knowledge.

body.translated_text: This is the supremely pure chanting of names (<s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s>) of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva</s>, the knowledge-body of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the knowledge-form of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Vajradhara</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, generating supreme delight and joy, for the purpose of purifying body, speech, and mind, for the complete purification of the accumulation of merit and knowledge for those who have not fulfilled the purification of the stages, for the attainment of the unattained supreme aim, for the attainment of what has not been attained, and for the comprehension of the <s>Dharma</s>-matrix of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — thus has it been taught, proclaimed, disclosed, analyzed, made clear, and empowered by me, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Vajradhara</s>, by the empowerment of the <s>Dharma</s>-nature of all <s>mantras</s> in your continuum and mind. These are the eleven words of the commendation of the first cycle.

body.text:
iyamasau vajrapāṇeḥ vajradharabhagavato jñānamūrteḥ sarvatathāgatajñānakāyasya mañjuśrījñānasattvasyāveṇikapariśuddhā nāmasaṃgitistavānuttaraprītiprāsādamahodvilya saṅjananārthahṃ, kāyavāṅmanoguhyapariśuddhyai, aparipūrṇapariśuddhabhūmiparimitāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāraparipūripariśuddhyai, anadhigatānuttarārthasyādhigamāya, aprāptasya prāptyai, yāvatsarvatathāgatasarvadharmanetrīsaṃdhāraṇārthaṃ ca mayā deśitā, saṃprakāśitā, vivṛtā, vibhajitottānikṛtā, adhiṣṭhatā cayaṃ mayā vajrapāṇe vajradhara tava santāne citte sarvamantradharmatādhiṣṭhāneneti || Mns_163 ||
iti prathamacakrasyeyamanuśaṃsā ekādaśa padāni

children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Vajradhara</s>,
delighted and satisfied, with palms joined,
bowing to the protector, the perfectly awakened one,
the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
together with many other protectors,
lords of the secret, <s>Vajrapāṇis</s>,
along with the kings of wrath,
spoke aloud these words:
"We rejoice, O Protector!
Excellent, excellent, well spoken!
A great purpose has been accomplished for us,
one that leads to perfect awakening.
And for the world, which is without a protector,
longing for the fruit of liberation,
this is the purified path to the highest good,
proclaimed through the method of the net of <s>māyā</s>.
Profound, noble, and vast,
of great purpose, accomplishing the world's aim,
this is indeed the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
spoken by the perfectly awakened one."

body.translated_text: Thus end the five concluding verses.

body.text: ārthamāyājālaṣoḍaśasāhāsrikān mahāyogatantrāntaḥ pātisamādhijālapaṭalād bhagavatā śrīśākyamuninā bhāṣitā bhagavato mañjuśrījñānasattvasyādvayaparamārtha nāmasaṃgītiḥ parisamāptā |
body.translated_text: From the chapter on the <s>Samādhijāla</s> (Net of Meditative Absorption) within the <s>Māyājālaṣoḍaśasāhasrika Mahāyogatantra</s>, this <s>Nāmasaṃgīti</s> (Chanting of Names) of the non-dual ultimate truth of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Mañjuśrī-jñānasattva</s>, spoken by the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Śrī Śākyamuni</s>, is completed.

body.text: ī. siṅ. likhyata, jayakarta, yavadvīpa, saṃ. 1423
